promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 8 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Last week ended after one run because a cold turned into a fever, so recovery now matters more than mileage. Next week is two short, easy walk-run sessions with full rest between, and the two missed runs are not made up.

flags.title: Missed runs
flags.detail: the Wed Sep 9 and Sat Sep 12 sessions were skipped during the illness, and they are not added back.

flags.title: Still unwell
flags.detail: you have been fever-free only since Friday, and you are still coughing and congested, so every run next week depends on how you feel that morning.

flags.title: Sleep and fatigue
flags.detail: you averaged 6 hours of sleep and feel wiped out, which slows recovery more than the runs do.

flags.title: Return load
flags.detail: next week totals 40 minutes of running, about half of the 75 minutes planned for last week, so the body can rebuild first.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No, not all three runs, and the two missed runs should not be added on top. Next week has two short sessions, Wed and Sat, and you run them only if you feel up to it.

Catch-up runs add load while your body is still recovering from a fever, and a setback would cost you more time than the missed runs did. The missed sessions are lost. The build comes back through steady weeks, not by squeezing in make-up runs.

new.analysis:
The week came apart after one session. Monday's walk-run went as planned: 24 minutes of 2-minute runs with 1-minute walks, at effort 6/10 with heart rate flat across the run. The cold started on Tuesday, and the next two planned runs were skipped.

| Day | Planned | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mon Sep 7 | Walk-run, 24 min | Done: 2.78 km in 23m 59s |
| Wed Sep 9 | Walk-run, 24 min | Missed |
| Sat Sep 12 | Walk-run, 27 min | Missed |

The four rest days were taken as rest, and nothing was overrun. The Monday run was done before the illness and was controlled, so it does not explain the week. The missed sessions were a result of being unwell, not of the plan being too hard.

Your heart rate averaged 139 with a maximum of 146, which is about 76 percent of your maximum of 182. The run segments held about 7:40 per km and the walks about 11:30 per km. That is a comfortable pace for where you are, so the plan does not need changing for speed.

A fever of 38.4 and a cough that is still there mean the first job is getting well. Two 20-minute sessions with rest days between keep the running easy and let you judge how you feel on each morning. If symptoms return or worsen, the right move is to skip the session, not to push through it.

Your goal is to run the whole 5K, and you are at 2-minute runs with 1-minute walks. That gap closes over several weeks of steady running, so a lost week is recoverable if you come back gradually. Once you are clear of symptoms, the following weeks add run time slowly, with a lighter week every three or four weeks.

safetyCallouts.title: A recent fever and ongoing cough need a professional check.
safetyCallouts.body: See a doctor or pharmacist if the fever returns, your breathing feels hard, you get chest tightness, or the cough and congestion are not clearing.

safetyCallouts.title: Skip running while you have a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: Restart only when you feel well, and stop a session if chest tightness, dizziness or breathlessness starts.
